question: Which external sources hold free-to-use pictures of the catalogue's kinds, and what did each actually yield?
licence_rule: Accepted: CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA. Refused by validate.py: any NC or ND licence.

sources.probe: systematic: 14 name/alias/extra terms × 87 kinds = ~1,200 searches; 9,387 free files returned, 1,735 naming a kind by loose match; re-scored with whole-word rules; 55 leads reviewed on contact sheets by eye
sources.yield: 33 verified pictures for 13 kinds (incl. first pictures for hun-phayon, mit-mo, waan; +8 somdej; 4 Phra Kring; 3 Chiang Saen; 2 takrut tubes)
sources.verdict: the main vein; automated matching is unsafe (waan→Cantonese street names, rajah→pitcher plant, bua→Swedish church) so every pick was looked at

sources.probe: 15 words × 17 places; 533 open records with media
sources.yield: 8 CC0 photographs from the Swedish Museum of Ethnography's 1887 Bangkok purchases: 6 child's modesty plates (a NEW kind, จะปิ้ง), 1 takrut pair on its waist cord, 1 tied stack of yantra sheets
sources.verdict: one real find; the Dutch and Swedish world-culture museums' amulets are mostly Sulawesi, Borneo and Bali child amulets, not our kinds

sources.yield: 0 — CC0 hits are Chinese steles, Thai Buddha heads, Borobudur; 'amulet Thailand' returns 10 records, none an amulet with an image
kris/keris only (130), a kind already capped

sources.probe: 36 kinds mapped to QIDs by label search
sources.yield: 0 usable — label search lands on wrong entities (a film, a village, a beetle); the right QIDs have no depicts files
sources.verdict: needs hand-curated QIDs to be worth anything

sources.access: API; anonymous use blocked by a Cloudflare challenge after ~25 calls; registered key = 10,000/day, needs an email-verification click
sources.yield: counts only: 'thai amulet' 32, 'amulet thailand' 40, 'phra somdej' 37, 'พระสมเด็จ' 21, 'tha phra chan' 19, 'burmese nat' 70, 'jimat' 22, 'kris dagger' 134, 'nang kwak' 7, 'takrut' 7, 'bagua mirror' 8 — CC0/BY/BY-SA, mostly Flickr photographs not on Commons
sources.verdict: the largest untapped pool of amateur photographs of amulets in hand and on stalls; blocked on one free registration (Nan)

sources.licence: their own free-to-use licences (not CC; commercial use allowed, resale barred)
sources.yield: unmeasured; likely a few dozen 'Thai amulet' stock photos
sources.verdict: would need the allowlist widened to their licences; Nan's call

sources.yield: a large Thai amulet holding, unmeasured
sources.verdict: NC conflicts with the register's paid-claim revenue; excluded unless Nan decides otherwise

sources.source: Penn Museum, Yale Peabody, Walters, LACMA
sources.access: no usable API (Cloudflare challenge / JS search)

sources.source: Old printed plates (Coedès 1926 'Siamese votive tablets', JSS)
sources.licence: public domain in Thailand (life+50) and the US (pre-1929); not in the EU until 2040
sources.verdict: usable with a jurisdiction note; not done — Nan's call

forks_for_nan.chore: one free registration with an email-verification click
forks_for_nan.stakes: unlocks the largest pool of CC photographs of amulets in hand, on stalls and in cases — the pictures a Lens arrival most resembles; without it the bank stays museum-and-Commons flavoured
forks_for_nan.worst_case_if_never: nothing breaks; coverage of the 30 picture-less kinds stays at zero until Nan photographs them

forks_for_nan.fork: Widen the allowlist to Unsplash/Pexels/Pixabay licences
forks_for_nan.stakes: a few dozen glossy stock photos; licences are free-to-use but not CC, so the site's 'CC0/BY/BY-SA only' promise would need rewording
museum-grade Thai amulet photographs; conflicts with dealer-paid claims on the register
the strongest bank possible and the only source for the 30 kinds nobody has photographed freely — a phone camera and an afternoon at Tha Phra Chan
